meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Who decided to give my son a zero before anyone spoke to him?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. What do you have?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. A student can write somewhere else and paste it in. Turn the screen.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. A paste would look exactly like that. Did you ask Owen where he wrote it before you entered the zero?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare. You skipped my question. Was Owen heard before the zero went in?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
A student is allowed to change his mind after an outline. Put both in front of me. And you've passed my question twice, Hale, so I'll take it Owen wasn't heard.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Fine. You did speak to him. A boy put on the spot by his teacher goes blank, but I'll read that note. What is it you want from this meeting?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in class is not a weekend at home. I asked what you want, and you gave me another exhibit.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that sells it says not to. So hand me the papers, all of them, and tell me where this ends.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

That's 4.4. He'll do it, to put this behind him and for no other reason: private, away from his class, nothing on his file, and all of it in writing tonight. Copies of every document you've described go in the same email.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Yes. Ten minutes. When does he write it, because his applications close December 1?
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, November 12, after school. Put the day and the room in tonight's email with the rest.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Thursday, and the copies of your documents. With those, yes.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
No. The email, tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite of his Hamlet essay on Thursday, November 12, after school, away from his class, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require that agreement in writing from you, with the room for Thursday and copies of every document you described to me. I expect that email tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight along with copies of every document you described. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.

What moved her: your dated note of the November 2 conversation with Owen, because it proved he was heard before the zero went in, which was the procedural point she was pressing hardest.

What cost ground: you passed over her question about whether Owen had been heard twice while adding new evidence, which made her shorter and let her assume the worst until you finally answered it.

What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history, with its edits between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, landed on exactly that kind of late October night, which is why she wrote the times down and went straight to procedure. It proves nothing about the essay. It is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: when she said a paste would look exactly like that, answer that defence on the spot and turn the screen to the version history before moving on to the quotation, so your strongest document stands before you add the next one.
